title: get_commit_scope: name the task's finalizing attempt so the wrapper owner guard stops scanning every .moe/attempts record
description:
Follow-up from QA of task-6aa460bb33184e1b84fc9c9e5c0a4560 (owner guard, approved 2026-10-29).

The owner guard in both wrappers decides on a foreign `finalizing` attempt by reading and parsing EVERY `.moe/attempts/*.json` record (sh `landing_owner_guard`, ps1 `Get-MoeOwnerGuard`). It does that on every landing where the task is unassigned or held by an unprotected owner, and that includes every worker completion, because complete_task clears the assignee. Closed attempts are never pruned: 584 records (579 closed) took 1.46 s on /mnt/d on 2026-10-29, and the count grows by one per claim.

The daemon already computes this hold (`util/claimEligibility.ts` `isHoldingFinalizingAttempt` / `foreignFinalizingAttempt`). An additive get_commit_scope field naming the task's well-formed finalizing attempt (`{attemptId, workerId, generation}` or null) would let each wrapper replace its ~12-line scan with one comparison. Wrappers keep the scan only when the field is absent (older daemon). Alternative: prune closed attempt records.
definitionOfDone: get_commit_scope returns an additive field naming the task's well-formed finalizing attempt (null when none), using the same predicate as claimEligibility, with daemon tests; docs/MCP_SERVER.md updated; cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test exits 0.

Both wrappers use the field when present and fall back to the current .moe/attempts scan only when it is absent; refusal codes and behaviour are unchanged; the shared postflight-owner-guard.cjs cases still pass in postflight.sh and postflight.ps1, and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes.

implementationPlan.description:
Tests first: the fake's new knob and four owner-guard cases.
(1) scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js, `case 'get_commit_scope'`. Add the knob FAKE_SCOPE_FINALIZING=computed|null|malformed.
- Read it with the existing `knob()` helper next to `ownershipMode`, before anything is written to stdout. A mistyped value then throws naming the knob, like the other knobs, and an empty value counts as unset.
- Unset or empty: serve NO finalizingAttempt key, as a daemon from before the field does. Every existing scenario then stays on the wrapper's legacy scan. scripts/tests/postflight-owner-scope.test.mjs, which deepStrictEquals the default reply, keeps passing unchanged; do not edit that file.
- `computed`, after `taskId` is known, mirrors finalizingAttemptsByTask (packages/moe-daemon/src/util/claimEligibility.ts) over .moe/attempts/*.json:
  - read the files in sorted name order, skipping any unreadable or unparsable file (try/catch per file);
  - keep records with phase === 'finalizing', taskId === taskId, a non-blank string id and workerId, and Number.isSafeInteger(generation) && generation >= 1;
  - the highest generation wins;
  - serve { attemptId: a.id, workerId: a.workerId, generation: a.generation }, or null when nothing qualifies.
- `null`: serve finalizingAttempt: null whatever the records say.
- `malformed`: serve the computed value with generation: String(generation), or the string 'null' when nothing qualifies. These are the coercion traps a wrapper must refuse, parallel to FAKE_SCOPE_OWNERSHIP_MODE=malformed.
- Place the key right after assigneeProtected in the ok({...}) object.
- Document the knob in the knob comment block, in the same style. Extend the sentence 'The ALIVE, PROTECTED and OWNERSHIP_MODE knobs accept only the values above' to cover FINALIZING.

(2) scripts/tests/postflight-owner-guard.cjs. Add four single cases right after ['finalizing', ...]:
- ['finalizing-field','architect',{FAKE_SCOPE_ASSIGNEE:'none',FAKE_SCOPE_FINALIZING:'computed'},{},[{id:'attempt-done',workerId:'worker-done',phase:'finalizing'}],ACTIVE]. The field names a foreign attempt, so the wrapper refuses.
- ['finalizing-own','architect',{FAKE_SCOPE_ASSIGNEE:'none',FAKE_SCOPE_FINALIZING:'computed'},{},[{id:'attempt-mine',workerId:'architect-og',phase:'finalizing'}],'']. The field names the caller's own attempt (wid is role+'-og'), so the wrapper lands. Every worker completion takes this path once the field exists.
- ['finalizing-null','architect',{FAKE_SCOPE_ASSIGNEE:'none',FAKE_SCOPE_FINALIZING:'null'},{},[{id:'attempt-done',workerId:'worker-done',phase:'finalizing'}],'']. The daemon's null wins over a disk record. This proves the guard no longer reads .moe/attempts when the field is present.
- ['finalizing-malformed','architect',{FAKE_SCOPE_ASSIGNEE:'none',FAKE_SCOPE_FINALIZING:'malformed'},{},[{id:'attempt-done',workerId:'worker-done',phase:'finalizing'}],ACTIVE]. A malformed field falls back to the scan, which still refuses.
Above them, add a two-line comment: a well-formed finalizingAttempt or null decides; only an absent or malformed one, or the disk fallback, scans .moe/attempts.
In single(), after assertRefused, assert for every refused case whose name starts with 'finalizing' (the existing 'finalizing' case included): `assert.ok(log.includes('attempt attempt-done of worker-done is still finalizing'), ...)`. The field path and the scan must give the same detail text.

The extra own-finalizing record and a foreign open record do not disturb a landing that passes the guard. This was probed on HEAD on 2026-10-30 for sh and ps1; ps1 Read-MoeAttempt's 'ambiguous or missing open attempt' only warns.

Red proof, before step 3:
`W=$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/d3cd-red-XXXX) && git archive HEAD scripts | tar -x -C $W && cp scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js scripts/tests/postflight-owner-guard.cjs $W/scripts/tests/ && mkdir $W/og && (cd $W && MOE_OWNER_GUARD_ONLY=finalizing-field,finalizing-own,finalizing-null,finalizing-malformed node scripts/tests/postflight-owner-guard.cjs sh $W/scripts/moe-agent.sh $W/scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js $W/og "$(command -v bash)"); echo RED_EXIT=$?; rm -rf $W`
It must fail at [finalizing-null], because today's scan refuses. Record that in the step note.

In the python verdict(), after the owner checks and right before the `for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(project, '.moe', 'attempts', '*.json')))` loop, insert:
```python
    fa = d.get('finalizingAttempt')
    if fallback != '1' and 'finalizingAttempt' in d and (fa is None or (isinstance(fa, dict)
            and isinstance(fa.get('attemptId'), str) and fa['attemptId'].strip()
```

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/moe-agent.ps1: the twin of step 3.
(a) Add `FinalizingSet = $false; Finalizing = $null` next to `OwnerSet = $false; Owner = $null; Protected = $null` in BOTH scope hashtables: Get-MoeDiskScope and the rpc branch of Get-MoeCommitScope.
(b) In Get-MoeCommitScope, after the `$ap = $resp.PSObject.Properties['assigneeProtected']...` line, add:
```powershell
        # Raw, for Get-MoeOwnerGuard: JSON null (nothing finalizing) and an absent key (older daemon) differ.
        $fp = $resp.PSObject.Properties['finalizingAttempt']; if ($fp) { $scope.FinalizingSet = $true; $scope.Finalizing = $fp.Value }
```
(c) In Get-MoeOwnerGuard, after the owner checks and right before `$files = @()`, add:
```powershell
        # get_commit_scope.finalizingAttempt decides when it is null or well-formed; an absent or
        # malformed field (older daemon) or the disk scope falls back to the records scan below.
        $fa = $s.Finalizing; $faId = Get-MoeProp $fa 'attemptId'; $faW = Get-MoeProp $fa 'workerId'
        if ($s.Source -eq 'rpc' -and $s.FinalizingSet -and ($null -eq $fa -or ($fa -is [System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject] -and
                $faId -is [string] -and $faId.Trim() -and $faW -is [string] -and $faW.Trim() -and (Test-MoeGeneration (Get-MoeProp $fa 'generation'))))) {
            if ($null -ne $fa -and $faW -cne $WorkerId) { $g.Code = $active; $g.Detail = "attempt $faId of $faW is still finalizing"; return $g }
            $g.Code = ''; $g.Detail = ''; return $g
        }
```
Keep the existing scan unchanged after it, as the fallback.
Why these forms:
- Get-MoeProp yields $null for a [string] 'null' or for a PSCustomObject without the property, so a malformed field falls through to the scan instead of throwing into the catch, where it would become OWNER_UNKNOWN.
- Test-MoeGeneration accepts only an [int] or [long] in 1..2^53-1. PowerShell would coerce '3' -gt 0 to true; this rejects it.
- -cne keeps the comparison case-sensitive, like the scan's `$w -cne $WorkerId`.
The outer try/catch stays the error-handling path: any throw is MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_OWNER_UNKNOWN. The detail string must stay byte-identical to sh's.

Field contract: `finalizingAttempt: {attemptId, workerId, generation} | null`. It names the attempt finalizingAttemptsByTask selects, whoever holds it, including the caller.

Wrapper rule:
- null → no finalizing hold.
- A well-formed value naming another worker → MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_ACTIVE_ASSIGNEE with the existing detail text.
- The caller's own attempt → lands.
- An absent field (older daemon), a malformed value or the disk fallback → the existing .moe/attempts scan, unchanged.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Pruning closed attempt records (the task's alternative) was rejected. attempts/ are durable delivery records, and pruning still leaves a disk scan in two wrappers; the field makes the guard O(1) and reuses the claim hold's predicate. A fake that serves the field by default was rejected because postflight-owner-scope.test.mjs deepStrictEquals the default reply. Gating it behind a knob keeps that file untouched and keeps every legacy scenario on the fallback scan. The daemon field was split into task-a2a55bc6, which keeps this task at 5 files and lets the field land without the merge gate.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The owner-guard functions are byte-identical in HEAD and the pending merge 3f6817f1; the merge rewrites other hunks of the same files, hence the step-1 merge gate. openClaimAttempt closes whatever attempt is open before it opens one, so a task holds at most one finalizing attempt, and the field names the same record the scan refuses on. With two open records, ps1 Read-MoeAttempt throws 'ambiguous or missing open attempt' but only warns: a checkpoint still lands (probed on HEAD 2026-10-30, sh and ps1). moe-agent.ps1 has no Set-StrictMode; Get-MoeProp is still the safe accessor. The sh disk fallback copies only assignedWorkerId from the task record, never finalizingAttempt.
planningNotes.risks: (1) Comparing the wrong id, or treating any present object as foreign, would refuse every worker completion, since complete_task leaves the task unassigned with the worker's own attempt finalizing. finalizing-own guards against this. (2) Treating a malformed field as null would land over a foreign finalizing attempt; finalizing-malformed guards against this. (3) PowerShell coerces '3' -gt 0 to true; only Test-MoeGeneration's type check rejects a string generation. (4) A shared file dirty at claim time: the peer gate blocks rather than landing a peer's hunks. (5) The ps1 legs need WSLENV forwarding, or postflight.ps1 runs ~12 minutes.
